items.stem:
Carbon compounds
(i) are good conductors of electricity.
(ii) are bad conductors of electricity.
(iii) have strong forces of attraction between their molecules.
(iv) have weak forces of attraction between their molecules.
The correct statements are
items.answer: (c) (ii) and (iv). Carbon compounds are bad conductors of electricity because they contain covalent bonds. The forces of attraction between their molecules are not very strong and they do not conduct electricity in the solid state, the molten state or in solution.

(ii) are poor conductors of electricity
(iii) have strong forces of attraction between their molecules

items.answer: (d) (ii) and (iv). Carbon compounds are covalent, so they are poor conductors of electricity and the forces of attraction between their molecules are weak.

items.stem: What is a homologous series of carbon compounds? Give an example and list its three characteristics.
items.answer: A homologous series is a group of organic compounds having similar structures and similar chemical properties in which the successive compounds differ by a —CH₂ group. Example : the alkane series CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈, C₄H₁₀ … Characteristics : (i) successive members differ by one —CH₂ unit, i.e. by a mass of 14 u; (ii) all members contain the same functional group and can be represented by one general formula, so they show similar chemical properties; (iii) physical properties such as melting point, boiling point and density change gradually with increasing molecular mass.

items.stem: Why does carbon exhibit tetra covalency?
items.answer: Carbon has four valence electrons, so its valency is four. Carbon cannot lose four electrons to form a C⁴⁺ ion because that requires a very large amount of energy, which cannot be supplied to the atom; nor can it gain four electrons to form a C⁴⁻ ion, because a nucleus of only 6 protons cannot hold 10 electrons. This is why carbon can only complete its octet by sharing its four valence electrons, i.e. it exhibits tetra covalency.

items.stem: Write the electronic dot structures of (a) F₂ (b) NH₃ (c) CCl₄
items.answer:
(a) F₂ : each fluorine atom has seven valence electrons; the two atoms share one electron pair (F : F), so each fluorine has a complete octet with three lone pairs.
(b) NH₃ : nitrogen has five valence electrons; it shares three of them with three hydrogen atoms to give three N—H shared pairs and one lone pair on nitrogen.
(c) CCl₄ : carbon shares each of its four valence electrons with one chlorine atom, giving four C—Cl shared pairs; each chlorine also carries three lone pairs.

items.stem: Mention the position of carbon on the basis of its electronic configuration and comment on the nature of the compounds formed by carbon.
items.answer: Carbon has atomic number 6, so its configuration is C(6) = 1s², 2s²2p². As it has four valence electrons, it is an element of group 14 and period 2. It can form only covalent compounds, because gaining or losing 4 electrons is impossible for it on the basis of the energy change during bond formation. So carbon always forms covalent compounds by sharing its valence electrons.

items.stem: What are soaps chemically? How do they differ from synthetic detergents?
items.answer: Chemically, soap is the sodium or potassium salt of a fatty acid (a long-chain carboxylic acid). Detergents are the ammonium or sulphonate salts of long-chain carboxylic acids.

items.stem: Give reasons for the following : Unsaturated hydrocarbons show addition reactions but saturated hydrocarbons do not.
items.answer: Unsaturated hydrocarbons have either double or triple bonds, one or two components of which break easily and are weak enough to form single covalent bonds with the added molecule. In comparison, saturated hydrocarbons have only single bonds, which are strong. This is why unsaturated hydrocarbons show addition reactions but saturated hydrocarbons do not.

items.stem: How is it that we can use detergents for washing clothes even when the water is hard, but not soaps? What change has been made in the composition of detergents to make them biodegradable?
items.answer: Detergents are sodium salts of sulphonic acids. They can be used for washing clothes even when the water is hard, because their calcium and magnesium salts are soluble in water. Soaps are sodium salts of fatty acids; they react with Ca²⁺ or Mg²⁺ ions to form salts which are insoluble in water and form scum. To make detergents biodegradable their hydrocarbon chains are made linear (unbranched), so micro-organisms can decompose them.

items.stem: 'Carbon forms strong bonds with most other elements making the compounds exceptionally stable.' Give reason to justify this statement.
items.answer: Carbon has 4 electrons in its outermost shell and requires 4 more electrons to attain a noble gas electronic configuration. It cannot form a positive ion, because a huge amount of energy is required to remove 4 valence electrons and the ion so formed would have 6 protons and only 2 electrons, making it highly unstable. It cannot form a negative ion either, because a nucleus with only 6 protons cannot hold 10 electrons against the inter-electronic repulsion. So carbon achieves a noble gas configuration only by sharing its 4 valence electrons with other atoms, forming strong covalent bonds. The two main reasons carbon forms a large number of such stable compounds are: (a) Catenation – the ability of carbon to form bonds with other carbon atoms, giving long chains, branched chains and rings; (b) Tetravalency – carbon has 4 valence electrons, so it can form covalent bonds with 4 other atoms.

items.stem: Write the chemical formula and name of the compound which is the active ingredient of all alcoholic drinks. List its two uses. Write chemical equation and name of the product formed when this compound reacts with (i) sodium metal (ii) hot concentrated sulphuric acid.
items.answer: The active ingredient of alcoholic drinks is ethanol; its formula is C₂H₅OH. Two uses of ethanol: (1) it is used as a solvent in various industries; (2) it is used as an antiseptic solution. (i) Reaction with sodium metal: 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂. The product is sodium ethoxide, and hydrogen gas is evolved. (ii) Reaction with hot conc. H₂SO₄ (at 443 K): C₂H₅OH --conc. H₂SO₄--> CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O. The product is ethene; conc. H₂SO₄ acts as a dehydrating agent.
items.ocr: Reaction arrows restored. The printed sodium equation is unbalanced (C₂H₅OH + Na → C₂H₅ONa + H₂); balanced here. The printed label 'Sodium ethanoate' under C₂H₅ONa contradicts the product itself, which is sodium ethoxide; corrected.

items.stem: What is methane? Draw its electron dot structure. Name the type of bonds formed in this compound. Why are such compounds: (i) poor conductors of electricity? and (ii) have low melting and boiling points? What happens when this compound burns in oxygen?
items.answer: Methane is a hydrocarbon formed by the combination of carbon with hydrogen. Its molecular formula is CH₄ and it is a main greenhouse gas. In its electron dot structure the carbon atom shares one electron pair with each of four hydrogen atoms, so the type of bond formed in methane is the covalent bond. (i) Covalent compounds are poor conductors of electricity because they are formed by the sharing of electrons and have no free electrons (or ions) available to conduct electricity. (ii) They have weak forces of attraction between their molecules, so little energy is required to break these forces; hence they have low melting and boiling points. When methane burns in oxygen a combustion reaction takes place: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O + heat + light.
items.ocr: Printed combustion equation shows O₂ written over the arrow and is unbalanced; rewritten balanced as CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. Printed 'Methane s a hydrocarbon ormed by' repaired to 'is a hydrocarbon formed by'. Electron dot figure belongs to the worked solution, so no image is attached.

items.stem: (a) Why are most carbon compounds poor conductors of electricity? (b) Write the name and structure of a saturated compound in which the carbon atoms are arranged in a ring. Give the number of single bonds present in this compound.
items.answer: (a) Electricity is conducted by moving electrons (or ions). Carbon forms covalent bonds by sharing electrons, so carbon compounds do not have free electrons or ions and are therefore poor conductors of electricity. (b) Cyclohexane, C₆H₁₂, is a saturated compound in which the carbon atoms are arranged in a ring: six carbon atoms joined in a closed hexagonal ring, each carbon also carrying two hydrogen atoms. There are 6 carbon–carbon single bonds present in the ring of this compound.
items.ocr: Printed answer label 'd Electricity is conducted...' is a damaged '(a)'. The cyclohexane structure is a worked-solution figure, so no image is attached.

items.stem: A compound 'X' on heating with excess conc. sulphuric acid at 443 K gives an unsaturated compound 'Y'. 'X' also reacts with sodium metal to evolve a colourless gas 'Z'. Identify 'X', 'Y' and 'Z'. Write the equation of the chemical reaction of formation of 'Y' and also write the role of sulphuric acid in the reaction.
items.answer: X = CH₃CH₂OH (ethanol); Y = CH₂=CH₂ (ethene); Z = hydrogen gas, H₂. Formation of Y: CH₃CH₂OH --conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K--> CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O. With sodium metal: 2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂. Here concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent; it removes a water molecule from ethanol.

items.stem: You are given ball and stick models of six carbon atoms and fourteen hydrogen atoms and a sufficient number of sticks. In how many ways can one join the models of six carbon atoms and fourteen hydrogen atoms to form different molecules of C₆H₁₄?
items.answer: Five ways. C₆H₁₄ (hexane) has five structural isomers, so five types of molecules can be made with these balls and sticks. The five isomers are: n-hexane (CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃), 2-methylpentane, 3-methylpentane, 2,2-dimethylbutane and 2,3-dimethylbutane.

items.stem: Draw the structural formulae of all the possible isomers of the compound with the molecular formula C₃H₆O and also give their electron dot structures.
items.answer: There are two possible isomers of C₃H₆O: (i) propanal, C₂H₅CHO, i.e. CH₃–CH₂–CHO, in which the aldehyde (–CHO) group is at the end of the chain; and (ii) propanone, CH₃COCH₃, in which the carbonyl (>C=O) group is on the middle carbon. In their electron dot structures every C–H and C–C bond is one shared electron pair, while the carbon–oxygen bond of the carbonyl group is two shared electron pairs, the oxygen atom also carrying two lone pairs of electrons.

items.stem: Two carbon compounds A and B have the molecular formulae C₃H₈ and C₃H₆ respectively. (a) Which one of the two is most likely to show addition reaction? Justify your answer. (b) Explain with the help of chemical equation, how an addition reaction is useful in vegetable ghee industry.
items.answer: (a) C₃H₆ (compound B) will show the addition reaction, as it is an unsaturated hydrocarbon containing a carbon–carbon double bond. C₃H₆ reacts with hydrogen in the presence of a catalyst to give propane by adding one molecule of hydrogen across the double bond: C₃H₆ + H₂ → C₃H₈. (b) Vegetable oils contain long unsaturated carbon chains. Vegetable oil reacts with hydrogen in the presence of nickel as a catalyst to form vegetable ghee, which is a saturated compound: R–CH=CH–R + H₂ --Ni--> R–CH₂–CH₂–R, i.e. vegetable oil (unsaturated) + H₂ --Ni--> vegetable ghee (saturated).
items.ocr: The bank also prints an 'or' variant of this question ('...how an addition reaction is useful in industries'); the main wording is kept. The vegetable-oil equation prints as badly mangled LaTeX; rewritten from the labels 'Vegetable oil (Unsaturated)', 'Ni' and 'Vegetable ghee (Saturated)'.

items.stem: (a) Give chemical tests to detect the presence of (i) Ethanol (ii) Ethanoic acid. (b) Why is ethanoic acid called glacial acetic acid?
items.answer: (a) (i) Test for ethanol – reaction with sodium: reactive metals like Na liberate hydrogen gas, which is combustible and burns with a pop sound. 2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂O⁻Na⁺ + H₂(g) (sodium ethoxide). (ii) Test for ethanoic acid – esterification: esters are formed by the reaction of an acid with an alcohol, so on warming ethanoic acid with ethanol in the presence of a few drops of conc. H₂SO₄ a sweet, fruity smelling ester is obtained. CH₃COOH + CH₃CH₂OH --conc. H₂SO₄, Δ--> CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. (b) The melting point of pure ethanoic acid is 290 K, so it often freezes during winter in cold climates and looks like ice. This gives rise to its name, glacial acetic acid.
items.ocr: The esterification equation prints with a broken arrow and scrambled labels ('Acid / Ethanoic acid / Ethane', 'CH C - OCH CH₃'); rewritten as CH₃COOC₂H₅ from the reactants shown. Reaction arrows restored.

items.stem: What are micelles? How does the formation of a micelle help to clean the clothes?
items.answer: Soap molecules consist of two parts – one part is hydrophobic (the long hydrocarbon tail, which dissolves in oil and grease) and the other part is hydrophilic (the ionic head, which dissolves in water). When soap is dissolved in water it forms groups of many molecules known as micelles. In these groups the hydrophobic tails point into the interior of the group and the ionic ends lie on the surface, facing the water. Soap in the form of a micelle is able to clean a dirty cloth because the oily dirt is collected in the centre of the micelle, held by the hydrocarbon tails, while the ionic ends keep the micelle suspended in water. When the water is agitated, the dirt sticks to the micelles and is pulled away from the cloth; rinsing then washes the dirt-laden micelles away with the water and the cloth becomes clean.
items.ocr: The printed solution is cut off by a page break at 'When water is agitated, the dirt sticks to'; the sentence was completed from the cleansing-action explanation printed elsewhere in the same chapter. The micelle diagram is a worked-solution figure, so no image is attached.

items.stem: What is an oxidizing agent? What happens when an oxidizing agent is added to propanol? Explain with the help of a chemical equation.
items.answer: (i) An oxidising agent is a substance which can give oxygen to other substances (or remove hydrogen from them). (ii) When an oxidising agent such as alkaline KMnO₄ or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ is added to propanol, the propanol is oxidised to propanoic acid: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–OH --alkaline KMnO₄ or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇--> CH₃–CH₂–COOH (propanoic acid). (iii) So propanol is oxidised to propanoic acid.

items.stem: When ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid in the presence of conc. H₂SO₄, a substance with fruity smell is produced. Answer the following: (i) State the class of compounds to which the fruity smelling compounds belong. Write the chemical equation for the reaction and write the chemical name of the product formed. (ii) State the role of conc. H₂SO₄.
items.answer: (i) The fruity smelling compounds belong to the class of esters. CH₃COOH + CH₃CH₂OH --conc. H₂SO₄--> CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. The chemical name of the product formed is ethyl ethanoate. (ii) Conc. H₂SO₄ acts as a dehydrating agent; it helps in the removal of the water formed in the reaction and so drives the esterification forward.

items.stem: When ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid in the presence of conc. H₂SO₄, a substance with fruity smell is produced. Answer the following: (i) State the class of compounds to which the fruity smelling compounds belong. Write the chemical equation for the reaction and write the chemical name of the product formed. (ii) State the role of conc. H₂SO₄ in this reaction.
items.answer: (i) The class of compounds to which the fruity smelling compounds belong is esters. CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH --conc. H₂SO₄--> CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O; here ethanoic acid and ethanol give ethyl ethanoate (an ester). The solution also prints a second example: C₃H₇COOH + C₂H₅OH --conc. H₂SO₄--> C₃H₇COOC₂H₅ + H₂O, i.e. butanoic acid with ethanol. (ii) The role of conc. H₂SO₄ in this reaction is that of a catalyst.

items.stem: (i) Chemical properties of ethanol is different from methyl ethanoate. Justify the statement with proper reason. (ii) Methyl ethanoate is used in making perfume. Justify. (iii) Ethanol is converted into ethene with excess of hot concentrated H₂SO₄. Justify with the help of chemical equation.
items.answer: (i) Ethanol reacts with sodium metal to liberate hydrogen, whereas methyl ethanoate does not. The two differ in their functional group – ethanol has the alcoholic –OH group while methyl ethanoate has the ester –COO– group – and since the functional group decides the chemical behaviour, their chemical properties differ. (ii) Methyl ethanoate is an ester and it has a pleasant fruity smell, which is why it is used in making perfumes. (iii) CH₃CH₂OH --conc. H₂SO₄, Δ--> CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O. Ethanol gets dehydrated with excess hot conc. H₂SO₄ to form ethene and H₂O; conc. H₂SO₄ acts as a dehydrating agent.
items.ocr: The printed equation in (iii) shows 'conc. HNO₃' over the arrow, which contradicts both the question and the very next line of its own solution ('Ethanol gets dehydrated with conc. H₂SO₄'). The solution text wins: the reagent is conc. H₂SO₄. Arrow restored.

items.stem: (a) Define the term functional group. Identify the group present in the two structures printed below: (i) a carbon atom joined to two hydrogen atoms by single bonds and to an oxygen atom by a double bond (H–CHO); (ii) a CH₃ group joined to a carbon that is double bonded to one oxygen and single bonded to an –OH group (CH₃–COOH). (b) What happens when 5% alkaline KMnO₄ solution is added drop by drop to warm ethanol taken in a test tube? State the role of alkaline KMnO₄ solution in this reaction.
items.answer: (a) A functional group is an atom or group of atoms – the reactive part of a compound – which largely determines the chemical properties of that compound. (i) The structure is methanal, HCHO; the group present is the aldehyde group, –CHO. (ii) The structure is ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH; the group present is the carboxylic acid group, –COOH. (b) The pink colour of the alkaline KMnO₄ disappears as it is added drop by drop, because it oxidises the warm ethanol to ethanoic acid: CH₃CH₂OH + 2[O] --KMnO₄/KOH--> CH₃COOH + H₂O. Alkaline KMnO₄ acts as an oxidising agent.

items.stem: An organic compound with molecular formula C₃H₈O reacts with sodium metal to produce hydrogen gas. Deduce the possible structure of the compound. Write the balanced chemical equation of the reaction.
items.answer: Since the compound liberates hydrogen gas with sodium metal, it must contain the alcoholic –OH functional group. The possible structure of the compound is propanol: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–OH (each of the three carbon atoms completes four bonds, the end carbon carrying the –O–H group). 2CH₃CH₂CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂CH₂O⁻Na⁺ + H₂(g), i.e. propanol gives sodium propoxide and hydrogen gas.
items.ocr: The printed molecular formula lost its subscripts ('C H O'); restored to C₃H₈O from the worked solution, which identifies the compound as propanol. The printed solution labels the product 'sodium ethoxide'; from its own formula CH₃CH₂CH₂O⁻Na⁺ the product is sodium propoxide, so the solution's formula wins. Printed 'Proanol' repaired to 'propanol'.

items.stem: Name the compound formed when ethanol is heated in excess of conc. sulphuric acid at 443 K. Also write the chemical equation of the reaction stating the role of conc. sulphuric acid in it. What would happen if hydrogen is added to the product of this reaction in the presence of catalysts such as palladium or nickel?
items.answer: When ethanol is heated in excess of conc. H₂SO₄ at 443 K, ethene is formed: CH₃CH₂OH --conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K--> CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O. Concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent, removing a molecule of water from ethanol. If hydrogen is then added to ethene in the presence of a catalyst such as palladium or nickel, an addition (hydrogenation) reaction takes place and ethane is formed: CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ --Ni or Pd (catalyst)--> CH₃–CH₃.
items.ocr: The printed solution says 'Ethene reacts with hydrogen ... to form ethene', but its own equation gives CH₃–CH₃; the solution's equation wins, so the product is ethane. Arrows restored.

items.stem: Write three different chemical reactions showing the conversion of ethanoic acid to sodium ethanoate. Write balanced chemical equation in each case. Write the name of the reactants and the products other than ethanoic acid and sodium ethanoate in each case.
items.answer: (1) With sodium hydroxide: CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O. Other reactant – sodium hydroxide (a base); other product – water. (2) With sodium metal: 2CH₃COOH + 2Na → 2CH₃COONa + H₂. Other reactant – sodium; other product – hydrogen gas. (3) With sodium carbonate: 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂. Other reactant – sodium carbonate; other products – water and carbon dioxide.
items.ocr: No year tag is printed with this answer. The printed answer block shows only two equations although the question asks for three, and its sodium equation is mis-set as '2CH₃COOH + 2Na → CH₃COONa + H₂O' (the sodium reaction gives H₂, not H₂O); balanced and corrected here. The third reaction, with sodium carbonate, is not legible in the scan and has been supplied so the answer covers the three conversions asked for.

items.stem: An organic acid X is a liquid which often freezes during winter time in cold countries. It has molecular formula C₂H₄O₂. On warming with ethanol in the presence of a few drops of conc. H₂SO₄ a compound Y with sweet smell is formed. (i) Identify X and Y. (ii) Write chemical equation for the reaction involved.
items.answer: (i) Compound X is CH₃COOH, ethanoic acid (glacial acetic acid) – it freezes in cold countries because its melting point is 290 K. Compound Y is CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ (CH₃COOC₂H₅), ethyl ethanoate, an ester with a sweet smell. (ii) CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH --conc. H₂SO₄--> CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O.

items.stem: Write chemical equations along with necessary conditions for the following changes to take place: (i) Ethanol to ethanoic acid. (ii) Ethanoic acid to sodium acetate. (iii) Methane to chloromethane.
items.answer: (i) CH₃CH₂OH --alkaline KMnO₄ + heat--> CH₃COOH (oxidation of ethanol to ethanoic acid). (ii) CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O (ethanoic acid with a base gives sodium acetate and water). (iii) CH₄ + Cl₂ --sunlight--> CH₃Cl + HCl (a substitution reaction in the presence of sunlight).

items.stem: (a) What is denatured alcohol? (b) How many covalent bonds does a molecule of ethane (C₂H₆) have? Draw its structure to justify your answer.
items.answer: (a) When ethanol is mixed with methanol or with some poisonous substances such as copper sulphate, pyridine etc., it becomes unfit for drinking. Such an alcohol is called denatured alcohol. (b) A molecule of ethane has seven single covalent bonds – one C–C bond and six C–H bonds. Structure: H₃C–CH₃, i.e. H–C(H)(H)–C(H)(H)–H, in which each carbon atom is joined to three hydrogen atoms and to the other carbon atom.

items.stem: (a) Complete the following reactions and name the main product formed in each case: (i) CH₃CH₂OH --alkaline KMnO₄--> (ii) CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH --> (iii) CH₄ + Cl₂ --sunlight-->
items.answer: (i) CH₃CH₂OH --alkaline KMnO₄ + heat--> CH₃COOH. Main product: ethanoic acid (acetic acid); ethanol is oxidised. (ii) CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH → CH₃COONa + C₂H₅OH. Main products: sodium ethanoate and ethanol; this alkaline hydrolysis of an ester is called saponification. (iii) CH₄ + Cl₂ --sunlight--> CH₃Cl + HCl. Main product: chloromethane (methyl chloride), along with hydrogen chloride; this is a substitution reaction.

items.stem: An organic compound X is an essential constituent of wine and beer. X is responsible for the intoxication caused by these drinks. Oxidation of X yields an organic acid Y which is present in vinegar. Name the compounds X and Y and write their structural formulae.
items.answer: The compound X is ethanol, C₂H₅OH, while Y is ethanoic acid (acetic acid), CH₃COOH. Structural formulae: ethanol – H₃C–CH₂–O–H, each carbon completing four bonds with hydrogen atoms; ethanoic acid – H₃C–C(=O)–O–H, in which the carboxyl carbon is doubly bonded to one oxygen and singly bonded to the –OH group. The conversion is an oxidation: CH₃CH₂OH --alkaline KMnO₄ (or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇)--> CH₃COOH.

items.stem: (a) Draw the structure of ethyne (C₂H₂). (b) List any two differences between soaps and detergents.
items.answer: (a) Ethyne: H–C≡C–H. The two carbon atoms are joined by a triple bond (three shared electron pairs) and each carbon atom is joined to one hydrogen atom by a single bond. (b) (i) Soaps are sodium salts of long chain fatty acids, whereas detergents are sodium or potassium salts of sulphonic acids of long chain hydrocarbons. (ii) Soaps cannot be used with hard water (they form scum), but detergents work well with both hard and soft water.

items.stem: (i) Define a homologous series of carbon compounds. (ii) Why are the melting and boiling points of C₄H₈ higher than those of C₃H₆ or C₂H₄? (iii) Why do we not see any gradation in the chemical properties of the compounds of a homologous series? (iv) Write the name and structure of (a) an aldehyde and (b) a ketone with the molecular formula C₃H₆O.
items.answer:
(i) A homologous series is a series of compounds with the same general formula and the same functional group, in which any two adjacent members differ by one –CH₂– unit, i.e. by 14 mass units.
(ii) C₂H₄, C₃H₆ and C₄H₈ belong to the same homologous series. As the molecular mass increases along a homologous series a gradation in physical properties is seen: melting and boiling points increase with increasing molecular mass, so C₄H₈ melts and boils at a higher temperature than C₃H₆ or C₂H₄.
(iii) The functional group is the same in every member of a homologous series, and the chemical properties are decided by the functional group, so no gradation in chemical properties is seen.
(iv) (a) Aldehyde: CH₃–CH₂–CHO (propanal)
    (b) Ketone: CH₃–CO–CH₃ (propanone)
items.ocr: LaTeX rewritten to Unicode. The printed definition reads 'differ by CH₂ 14 mass unit'; given here as one –CH₂– unit (14 u). The displayed structures of propanal and propanone were badly broken by OCR (propanal drawn with four carbons), so both are given in condensed form consistent with C₃H₆O.

items.stem: (i) Write the name and structure of an organic compound 'X' having two carbon atoms in its molecule and whose name is suffixed with '-ol'. (ii) What happens when 'X' is heated with excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K? Write the chemical equation for the reaction, stating the conditions for the reaction. Also state the role played by concentrated sulphuric acid in the reaction. (iii) Name and draw the electron dot structure of the hydrocarbon produced in the above reaction.
items.answer:
(i) X is ethanol, CH₃–CH₂–OH (H–CH₂–CH₂–O–H drawn out as H–C(H)(H)–C(H)(H)–O–H).
(ii) When ethanol is heated with excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K it loses a molecule of water and gives ethene:
CH₃CH₂OH ─(hot conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K)→ CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O
(ethanol → ethene). The concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent, removing water from the ethanol.
(iii) The hydrocarbon produced is ethene. In its electron dot structure each carbon shares two electron pairs with the other carbon (a C=C double bond) and one electron pair with each of two hydrogen atoms, so every carbon completes its octet and every hydrogen its duplet.

items.stem: The formulae of four organic compounds are given below: A: C₂H₄, B: CH₃COOH, C: C₂H₅OH, D: C₂H₆. (i) Which one of these compounds A, B, C or D is a saturated hydrocarbon? (ii) Identify the organic acid and give its structural formula. (iii) Which of the above compounds, when heated at 443 K in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄, forms ethene as the major product? What is the role played by concentrated H₂SO₄ in this reaction? Also write the chemical equation involved. (iv) Give a chemical equation for the reaction of B and C with each other in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄. Name the major product formed and mention one of its important uses.
items.answer:
(i) D (C₂H₆, ethane) is the saturated hydrocarbon.
(ii) B (CH₃COOH) is the organic acid. Its structural formula is H–C(H)(H)–C(=O)–O–H, i.e. CH₃–COOH (ethanoic acid).
(iii) C (ethanol, C₂H₅OH) is the compound. Concentrated H₂SO₄ acts as a dehydrating agent and removes a molecule of water from ethanol:
C₂H₅OH ─(hot conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K)→ C₂H₄ (ethene) + H₂O
(iv) CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ─(conc. H₂SO₄)→ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O
(ethanoic acid + ethanol → ethyl ethanoate). The major product is the ester ethyl ethanoate, which is used in making perfumes and as a flavouring agent.

(c) Would you be able to check if water is hard by using a detergent? Give a reason to justify your answer.
items.answer:
(a) X is ethene (C₂H₄) and Y is ethane (C₂H₆), whose molecular mass is 30 g mol⁻¹.
CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ ─(Ni or Pd)→ CH₃–CH₃

(b) (i) Butanone: CH₃–CO–CH₂–CH₃

items.stem: Compare soaps and detergents on the basis of their composition and their cleansing action in hard water.
items.answer:
Composition: soaps are the sodium or potassium salts of long chain carboxylic (fatty) acids, whereas detergents are the ammonium or sulphonate salts of long chain carboxylic acids.
Cleansing action in hard water: hard water contains calcium and magnesium salts. These react with soap and form an insoluble white curdy substance called scum, so a large amount of soap is wasted, little lather is formed and the cleansing action is hindered. The charged ends of a detergent do not form an insoluble precipitate with the calcium and magnesium ions of hard water, so detergents lather and clean effectively in hard water as well as in soft water.

items.stem: (a) Write the names and structures of (i) an alcohol and (ii) an aldehyde with four carbon atoms in their molecules. (b) List two differences between saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons.
items.answer:
(a) (i) The alcohol with four carbon atoms is butanol: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–OH.
    (ii) The aldehyde with four carbon atoms is butanal: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CHO.
(b) Hydrocarbons in which all the consecutive carbon atoms are linked by single bonds are called saturated hydrocarbons; those in which the consecutive carbon atoms are linked by at least one double or triple bond are called unsaturated hydrocarbons. Two differences follow from this:
(i) Type of carbon-carbon bond: saturated hydrocarbons have only single covalent bonds, while unsaturated hydrocarbons have at least one double or triple bond.
(ii) Reactivity and stability: saturated hydrocarbons are less reactive and more stable, while unsaturated hydrocarbons are more reactive and less stable. (Their general formulae also differ: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ for alkanes against CₙH₂ₙ for alkenes and CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ for alkynes.)

items.stem: (a) Explain why carbon forms covalent bonds. Give two reasons for carbon forming a large number of compounds. (b) Explain the formation of an ammonia molecule.
items.answer:
(a) Carbon has the electronic configuration 2, 4. It could complete its octet either by gaining four electrons to form a C⁴⁻ anion or by losing four electrons to form a C⁴⁺ cation, but neither is possible on energy considerations - it would need a very large amount of energy to hold ten electrons on a small nucleus, or to remove four electrons. Carbon overcomes this problem by sharing its four valence electrons with other atoms, i.e. by forming covalent bonds. Carbon forms a very large number of compounds because of (i) catenation, its ability to link with other carbon atoms to give long chains, branched chains and rings, and (ii) tetravalency, its ability to bond with four other atoms.
(b) Formation of NH₃: the electronic configuration of nitrogen is 2, 5, so it needs three more electrons to complete its octet; the electronic configuration of hydrogen is 1, so each hydrogen needs one more electron to complete its duplet. One nitrogen atom therefore shares one electron pair with each of three hydrogen atoms, giving three N–H single covalent bonds and one lone pair on nitrogen.

items.stem: (a) Give a chemical test to distinguish between saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons. (b) Name the products formed when ethane burns in air. Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction, showing the types of energies liberated. (c) Why is the reaction between methane and chlorine in the presence of sunlight considered a substitution reaction?
items.answer:
(a) Bromine water test. Bromine water is a brown coloured liquid. Unsaturated hydrocarbons give an addition reaction with bromine, so the colour of bromine water is decolourised. Saturated hydrocarbons do not react with bromine water, so its colour is not decolourised.
(b) On burning ethane in air the products obtained are carbon dioxide and water, along with heat and light:
2C₂H₆(g) + 7O₂(g) → 4CO₂(g) + 6H₂O(l) + Heat + Light
(c) Methane reacts with chlorine in the presence of sunlight to form chloromethane and hydrogen chloride:
CH₄ + Cl₂ ─(sunlight)→ CH₃Cl + HCl
With excess chlorine all four hydrogen atoms of methane are replaced by chlorine atoms to form carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄). The reaction is considered a substitution reaction because the hydrogen of methane is substituted (replaced) by chlorine.

items.stem: Why are certain compounds called hydrocarbons? Write the general formula for the homologous series of alkanes, alkenes and alkynes and also draw the structure of the first member of each series. Write the name of the reaction that converts alkenes into alkanes and also write a chemical equation to show the necessary conditions for the reaction to occur.
items.answer:
Certain compounds are called hydrocarbons because they are formed mainly from carbon and hydrogen.
General formula for the homologous series of alkanes: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂; of alkenes: CₙH₂ₙ; of alkynes: CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.
First members: methane, CH₄ - one carbon atom joined to four hydrogen atoms by single bonds; ethene, CH₂=CH₂ - two carbon atoms joined by a double bond, each carrying two hydrogen atoms; ethyne, H–C≡C–H - two carbon atoms joined by a triple bond, each carrying one hydrogen atom.
Hydrogenation, an addition reaction, converts alkenes into alkanes:
CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ ─(Pt/Pd/Ni)→ CH₃–CH₃
Dihydrogen gas adds to an alkene in the presence of a finely divided catalyst such as platinum, palladium or nickel to form an alkane.

items.stem: Soaps and detergents are both types of salts. State the difference between the two. Write the mechanism of the cleaning action of soap. Why do soaps not form lather with hard water? Mention any two problems that arise due to the use of detergents instead of soaps.
items.answer:
Difference: soaps are sodium or potassium salts of long chain carboxylic acids, whereas detergents are ammonium or sulphonate salts of long chain carboxylic acids. Soaps have a lesser cleansing action than detergents, which clean better.
Cleansing action of soap: when soap is dissolved in water it forms a colloidal solution in which the soap molecules cluster together into micelles and remain radially suspended in water, with the hydrocarbon ends towards the centre and the ionic ends directed outward. Dirt particles adhere to the oily or greasy layer present on skin or clothes. When a dirty cloth is dipped into soap solution, the non-polar hydrocarbon ends of the micelles get attached to the grease or oil present in the dirt while the polar ionic ends remain in the water. The mechanical action of rubbing then dislodges the oily layer from the dirty surface, shaping it into small globules, and a stable emulsion of oil in water is formed. The emulsified oil or grease globules, bearing the dirt, can now be readily washed away with water on rinsing.
Soaps do not form lather with hard water because the calcium and magnesium salts present in hard water displace the sodium or potassium ions from the soap molecules, forming an insoluble substance called scum instead of lather.
Two problems that arise from using detergents instead of soaps: (i) detergents are not biodegradable, so they accumulate in the environment and cause pollution; (ii) the entry of detergents into the food chain leads to bioaccumulation in living beings and tends towards health issues.

items.stem: (a) Differentiate between esterification and saponification, giving one example of each. (b) Write any two advantages of detergents over soaps.
items.answer:
(a) Esterification: the process of formation of an ester by the reaction of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid.
CH₃–COOH + H–OCH₂CH₃ ─(conc. H₂SO₄, heat)→ CH₃–COOCH₂CH₃ + H₂O
(ethanoic acid, a carboxylic acid + ethanol, an alcohol → ethyl ethanoate, an ester)
Saponification: esters react in the presence of an acid or a base to give back the alcohol and the carboxylic acid (as its salt when a base is used). This reaction is known as saponification.
CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH → C₂H₅OH + CH₃COONa
(b) Advantages of detergents over soaps: (i) they can be used even in hard water; (ii) they can be used even in acidic medium; (iii) they produce lather much more easily than soaps; (iv) their cleansing power is much higher than that of soaps; (v) they are more soluble in water than soaps.

items.stem: (a) Why does carbon form the largest number of compounds? Give two reasons. (b) Why are some of these called saturated and the others unsaturated compounds? (c) Which of these two is more reactive and why? (d) Draw the structures of the following compounds: (i) Bromopentane (ii) Hexanal.

(a) Carbon forms a large number of compounds because of (i) Catenation - carbon forms bonds with other atoms of carbon, giving long chains, branched chains and rings; and (ii) Tetravalency - carbon shares its four valence electrons with four other atoms.

items.answer:
(a) (i) CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O; the main product is sodium ethanoate.

Characteristic features of covalent compounds: (i) they have low melting and boiling points; (ii) they are generally gaseous or liquid substances; (iii) they are bad conductors of electricity and heat; (iv) they are of two types, polar and non-polar.

items.stem: (a) Define catenation. Why does no other element exhibit catenation to the extent seen in carbon compounds? (b) Name the type of compound formed by the reaction of an organic acid and an alcohol. Write the chemical equation for the reaction involved.
items.answer:
(a) Catenation is the self-linking property of an element due to which a large number of its atoms can be linked with each other by covalent bonds to form a chain. No other element except carbon possesses this self-linking property to an extent that lets it form large compounds as long chains, so no other element exhibits catenation to the extent seen in carbon compounds.
(b) An ester is formed by the reaction of an organic (carboxylic) acid and an alcohol; the reaction is called esterification.
CH₃COOH + CH₃CH₂OH ─(conc. H₂SO₄)→ CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ + H₂O
(ethanoic acid + ethanol → ethyl ethanoate)

items.stem: (a) Amongst soaps and detergents, which can work effectively in hard water and why? (b) Name the salts which cause hardness of water. (c) What change will you observe if you test soap with litmus paper (red and blue)?
items.answer:
(a) Detergents work more effectively in hard water. They are ammonium or sulphonate salts of long chain hydrocarbons, and the charged ends of these compounds do not form an insoluble precipitate with the calcium and magnesium ions present in hard water, whereas soaps form an insoluble precipitate with hard water which hinders their cleansing action. Detergents therefore clean more effectively.
(b) The salts that lead to hardness of water are the chlorides and sulphates of calcium and magnesium, i.e. CaCl₂, MgCl₂, CaSO₄ and MgSO₄.
(c) Soap solution turns red litmus paper blue, while there is no effect on blue litmus paper. This indicates that soaps are basic in nature.

items.stem: Compound A (C₂H₆O) is obtained by reacting a compound B with water in the presence of phosphoric acid. A burns in air with a blue flame to form CO₂ and H₂O. On reacting with K₂Cr₂O₇ it produces compound C, which turns blue litmus red. Identify the compounds A, B and C. Write the chemical equations involved in all the reactions.
items.answer:
A is obtained by the addition of water to another compound B, so A is an alcohol and B is an alkene. With the given molecular formula C₂H₆O, A is ethanol and B is ethene; C, which turns blue litmus red, is ethanoic acid.

CH₃–CH₂–OH ─(K₂Cr₂O₇)→ CH₃COOH (ethanoic acid, C)

Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

R is an organic compound containing only carbon, chlorine and fluorine. It is produced as a volatile derivative of methane, ethane and propane. It has been widely used as refrigerant, propellent and solvent. Montreal protocol phased out manufacture of such compounds because R contributes to S in the atmosphere.

(i) What is ozone depletion?
(ii) Identify the labelled parts R and S in this passage.
(iii) Which of the following would not be a consequence of S?
(a) Increased rates of lung cancer
(b) Increased incidence of premature skin ageing
(c) Increased incidence of severe sunburns
(d) Increased incidence of cataracts
(iv) Montreal protocol was signed in which year?
(a) 1965
(b) 1987
(c) 2012
(d) 1999
items.answer:
(i) Ozone depletion means the thinning of the ozone layer in the atmosphere. Many chemicals, mainly CFCs, are responsible for it.
(ii) In the given passage, 'R' is chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) and 'S' is ozone depletion.
(iii) (a) Major consequences of ozone depletion are increased incidences of cataracts, severe sunburns, skin cancer and premature ageing of skin etc. UV rays do not affect respiratory organs.
(iv) (b) Montreal protocol was signed on 16 September, 1987.

Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

Carbon is so versatile in nature that organic chemistry forms a separate branch of chemistry which deals mainly with carbon and its compounds. Carbon is an element with symbol C, atomic number 6 and electronic configuration 2, 4. Carbon has a valency of four. So, it is capable of bonding with four other atoms of carbon or atoms of some other monovalent element. Compounds of carbon are formed with oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen, sulphur, chlorine and many other elements, giving rise to compounds with specific properties which depend on the elements other than the carbon present in the molecule.

(i) Write the name of the term used for four valency of carbon.
(ii) Name the term used to define property of carbon to form bond with another carbon atom.
(iii) Name the group and period to which carbon belong.
(iv) Which of the following statements is incorrect?
(a) Valence electrons of carbon are 4.
(b) Carbon has a valency of four.
(c) Organic chemistry forms a separate branch of chemistry which deals mainly with carbon and its compounds.
(d) Electronic configuration of carbon is 2, 6.
items.answer:
(i) The term used for four valency of carbon is tetravalency.
(ii) Catenation is the term used to define the property of carbon to form a bond with another carbon atom.
(iii) Carbon belongs to the second period and the fourteenth group of the periodic table.
(iv) (d) Total electrons present in carbon are 6. Out of these 6 electrons, 2 are present in the first shell and the other four in the next shell. This gives the electronic configuration of carbon as 2, 4. Hence, the incorrect option is (d).

Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

Ethanol or ethyl alcohol is an important organic compound. It burns in air to form carbon dioxide and water. It is used in industries, hospitals and homes. Ethanol is supplied to hospitals and research laboratories without charging different taxes. Therefore, to prevent its misuse for drinking, it is mixed with some poisonous chemicals. Drinking such an alcohol causes blindness, liver damage and even death.

(i) Based on the data represented in the bar graph given alongside, why is there a reduction in emission of carbon monoxide from vehicles when a mixture of petrol and ethanol was used as fuel?
(ii) Which substance is most commonly added to ethyl alcohol to make it unfit for drinking?
(iii) Which organ in human body is most affected by the excessive intake of alcoholic drinks?
(iv) Ethanol has no effect on litmus solutions. Why?
items.answer:
(i) Ethanol is a clean fuel because it gives only carbon dioxide and water on burning. It does not produce any poisonous gas like carbon monoxide. So, addition of ethanol to petrol has the advantage of reducing the emission of carbon monoxide from vehicles.
(ii) Methyl alcohol (methanol), a poisonous substance, is added to ethyl alcohol to make it unfit for drinking.
(iii) Liver is most affected by the excessive intake of alcoholic drinks.
(iv) Ethanol does not contain any hydrogen ions, so it is a neutral compound. Thus ethanol has no effect on any litmus solution.

Teacher asked Pawan to carry out the following practical step under his observation: Take about 10 mL of water each in two test tubes. Teacher said to Ganesh to do the following experiment. Take about 10 mL of distilled water (or rain water) and 10 mL of hard water (from a tubewell or hand-pump) in separate test tubes. Add a couple of drops of soap solution to both. Shake the test tubes vigorously for an equal period of time and observe the amount of foam formed.

(ii) In the test tube containing hard water.
(iii) Water containing soluble salts of Mg²⁺ and Ca²⁺ is called hard water.
(iv) Soap reacts with hard water to form scum and is used up in removing the hardness of the water. So lather is not formed with hard water and soap.
(v) Rain water is the purest form of water found in nature.

Teacher said to Raheem to do the following experiment: Take two test tubes with about 10 mL of hard water in each. Add five drops of soap solution to one and five drops of detergent solution to the other. Shake both test tubes for the same period.

(ii) In which test tube is a curdy solid formed?
(iii) What are detergents?
(iv) Which will form foam with hard water easily, soap or synthetic detergent?

Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

The two characteristic features seen in carbon, that is, tetravalency and catenation, put together give rise to many compounds. Many compounds have different atoms or group of atoms attached to different carbon chains.

(i) Draw the structure of the hydrocarbon containing four carbon atoms with single bonds and open chain structure, and with branched chain structure.
(ii) Define catenation.
(iii) Define functional group.
(iv) What are saturated hydrocarbons?
items.answer:
(i) (a) Open chain structure (butane): CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃
(b) Branched chain structure (2-methylpropane, iso-butane): CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₃
(ii) Catenation is the ability of a carbon atom to form bonds with other carbon atoms, linking them into long chains, branched chains and rings.
(iii) A functional group is an atom or group of atoms attached to the carbon chain of an organic compound which determines the properties of that compound.
(iv) Saturated hydrocarbons are those hydrocarbons which contain only carbon–carbon single bonds.

Ethanol is a liquid at room temperature. Ethanol is commonly called alcohol and is the active ingredient of all alcoholic drinks. It is also used as a solvent in medicines such as tincture of iodine and cough syrup. Ethanol reacts with sodium as well as with carboxylic acids. Ethanol can also undergo dehydration in the presence of sulphuric acid.

(i) What happens when ethanol is strongly heated in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄?
(ii) Write the chemical equation when ethanol reacts with sodium metal.
(iii) Write the molecular formula of ethanol and draw its structural formula.
(iv) What do you mean by denatured alcohol?
items.answer:
(i) Ethanol forms ethene by dehydration.
CH₃–CH₂OH →(hot and conc. H₂SO₄) CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O
(ii) 2CH₃–CH₂–OH + 2Na → 2CH₃–CH₂ONa + H₂
H₂ gas is evolved.
(iii) Molecular formula: C₂H₅OH. Structural formula: H₃C–CH₂–O–H (each carbon carrying its hydrogens, with the –OH group on the terminal carbon).
(iv) Alcohol which is made unfit for drinking purposes is called denatured alcohol. This is done by adding poisonous substances such as methanol, or by adding copper sulphate to colour it.

Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

Carboxylic acids are a class of organic compounds containing the –COOH functional group. The first member of the carboxylic acid homologous series is formic acid. Carboxylic acids are weak acids, but react with sodium hydroxide, alcohols, metals, etc.

(i) Complete the following equation with the appropriate compound: CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ →
(ii) Draw the electron dot structure of ethanoic acid.
(iii) Methanoic acid is produced during a bee sting and causes irritation. How will you neutralize this?
(iv) What is esterification?
items.answer:
(i) CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂
(ii) In the electron dot structure of ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH), the methyl carbon shares one electron pair with each of three hydrogens and one with the carboxyl carbon; the carboxyl carbon shares two pairs with one oxygen (C=O) and one pair with the –O–H oxygen, which in turn shares a pair with hydrogen.
(iii) We neutralize methanoic acid by applying a weak base such as NaHCO₃ (baking soda).
HCOOH + NaHCO₃ → HCOONa + H₂O + CO₂
(iv) Esterification is the reaction of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid to give a sweet-smelling compound called an ester.
CH₃COOH + CH₃CH₂OH →(conc. H₂SO₄) CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ + H₂O

Soaps are sodium or potassium salts of long chain carboxylic acids. The action of soaps and detergents is based on the properties of both hydrophobic and hydrophilic groups in the molecule and this helps to emulsify the oily dirt and hence its removal.

Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

Compounds having carbon atoms among the components are known as carbon compounds. Carbon compounds could only be obtained from a living source; hence they are also known as organic compounds. Bond formed by sharing of electrons is called a covalent bond. Two or more atoms share electrons to make their configuration stable. In this type of bond, all the atoms have similar rights over the shared electrons. Compounds which are formed because of covalent bonds are called 'covalent compounds'. Covalent bonds are of three types: single, double and triple covalent bond. Carbon combines with oxygen, hydrogen, nitrogen, sulphur, chlorine and many other elements to form various stable compounds. The stability of carbon compounds is due to the small size of carbon which enables the nucleus to hold on to the shared pair of electrons strongly. The reactions shown by carbon compounds involve breaking of old bonds in the reacting molecules and the formation of new bonds in the product molecules. Carbon has the unique ability to form bonds with other atoms of carbon, giving rise to large molecules. This property is called catenation.

(i) Which of the following is true about saturated carbon compounds?
(a) Carbon compounds could only be obtained from a living source.
(b) Two or more atoms share electrons to make their configuration.
(c) Carbon giving rise to large molecules.
(d) Atoms are satisfied by forming single covalent bond.
(ii) What is catenation?
(a) It forms bonds with its bond only.
(b) Carbon decreases the molecules.
(c) Existence of an element is 2 or more forms.
(d) Carbon form bonds with other atoms of carbon.
(iii) What is a covalent bond?
(a) Compound contains five carbon atoms.
(b) Undergo substitution reactions with bond.
(c) Electrons shared between atoms to contribute an electron.
(d) Molecule adds on to the multiple bonds.
(iv) What do you mean by isomer?
(a) Atoms have similar rights over shared electrons.
(b) Atoms arising due to electron pair sharing.
(c) Two or more compounds having the same molecular formula.
(d) A three-dimensional structure.
items.answer:
(i) (d) Atoms are satisfied by forming single covalent bond.
(ii) (d) Carbon form bonds with other atoms of carbon.
(iii) (c) Electrons shared between atoms to contribute an electron.
(iv) (c) Two or more compounds having the same molecular formula.

Read the following case based passage and answer the questions given after passage.

In diamond, each carbon atom is bonded to four other carbon atoms by a single covalent bond. This is why a diamond is a rigid, compact, three dimensional structure and is very hard to break. It is a bad conductor of heat and electricity, as there are no free electrons present in it. On the other hand graphite contains free electrons, so it is a good conductor of heat and electricity. Lead pencils contain graphite encased in a wooden covering. A fullerene molecule consists of 60 carbon atoms arranged in pentagons and hexagons, like in a standard football. In carbon compounds, different compounds are formed with different structures with the same molecular formula. These compounds are called isomers and the phenomenon is called 'isomerism'. Carbon compounds in which all the four valencies of carbon atom are satisfied by forming single covalent bonds are known as saturated carbon compounds.

(i) Discuss why a diamond is a rigid, compact, three dimensional structure and is very hard to break.
(ii) What are saturated carbon compounds?
items.answer:
(i) In diamond each carbon atom is bonded to four other carbon atoms by strong single covalent bonds, forming a continuous three dimensional network. This rigid, compact giant structure is what makes diamond very hard and difficult to break.
(ii) Carbon compounds in which all the four valencies of the carbon atom are satisfied by forming single covalent bonds are called saturated carbon compounds.

(i) Draw the structure of the hydrocarbon with general formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ where n = 3.

items.answer:
(i) For n = 3, CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ gives C₃H₄, which is propyne. Its structure is H₃C–C≡C–H.
(ii) Hydrogenation reaction (an addition reaction).
